Domestic business sales increased to 825 crores from 774 crores in Q4 FY26, reflecting healthy demand across key customer segments.
EBITDA margin improved to 8% compared with 7.4% in Q4 FY26 and 6.9% in Q1 FY26.
Growth & demand: EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹94 crores, registering sequential growth of 10.1% and a year-on-year increase of 16.1%.
Profit before tax increased to ₹24 crores representing a QoQ growth of 33.5% and a YoY 6 | P a g e increase of 153.7%.
So, overall, if you look at the demand side, both international and domestic demand has been volatile, but domestic demand has been comparatively less volatile than international demand.
Margins & costs: Our emphasis on product mix optimization, discipline procurement and manufacturing efficiency enabled another quarter of improvement in operating profitability supporting higher gross margins and a stronger EBITDA performance.

Gross profit increased to ₹466 crores compared to ₹434 crores in the preceding quarter with gross profit margins expanding to 39.8% from 37.4% supported by favorable product realization, better inventory management and efficient raw material utilization.
And this ramp up of this PET project, like you had mentioned, ₹500 crores on a decent utilization with 15% EBITDA margin.

In fabric business, in denim, our capacity again has been in 90%, whereas in knit business, it has been in mid 80%.
So, this will have 50,000 metric ton per year capacity and we will be expecting a revenue of ₹500 Cr from the project which we are implementing 11 | P a g e as the first phase of B2B.
Balance sheet & cash: We continue to leverage our diversified product portfolio and integrated manufacturing capabilities to respond effectively to changing customer requirements while maintaining discipline on cost and capital allocation.

Moving to the operating level, Finance costs for the quarter stood at ₹31 crores compared with ₹30 crores in the preceding quarter, primarily attributable to the increase in working capital requirements.

The full-year finance cost for FY26 was ₹123 crores, down from ₹135 crores in FY25.
From the balance sheet perspective, our net worth increased to ₹1,372 crores in FY26, from ₹1,308 crores in FY25.
Growth & demand: Coming to the financial performance for Q4 FY26 , revenue from operations stood at ₹1,142 crores, registering quarter -over-quarter growth of 4.5%, while declining 9.1% year -over-year, primarily due to weaker export demand.
Our domestic sales remain relatively stable at ₹774 crores, reflecting resilience in the domestic market despite overall demand softness.
Registering a strong growth of ₹22 crores, a year-over-year growth of 74.5%, primarily driven from the gain from the sale of non -value assets.
Margins & costs: The impact has been visible in terms of volatility in the key raw material costs and has also significantly increased the other cost components, like dyes and chemical costs, freight costs, impacting the overall cost structure of all textile products.
On a year -on-year basis, costs were marginally lower by ₹1.5 crores, compared to ₹124.7 crores in Q4 FY25, indicating a stable input cost management despite the external volatility.
Our employee costs marginally increased by 1.8% year -over-year, while power and fuel costs reduced by 3.4% year -over-year, reflecting effective cost control.
Capex & expansion: The EBITDA stood at ₹327 crores, from ₹233 crores, registering a strong growth of 40.5% year -over- year, with margins improving to 7.1% from 4.8%, an expansion of 231 basis points.

Our financial assets have increased to ₹387 crores from ₹299 crores, primarily on account of the investment the company has done in Adani Power, and strengthening overall liquidity, indicating ongoing investment in the growth initiative.

Now, with a stronger balance sheet, improved cash flows, and continued investment in the modernisation of our plants, we believe the company is well-positioned to deliver steady revenue growth and margin expansion in FY27.

Total borrowing reduced to 7 | P a g e ₹1,510 crores from ₹1,621 crores year -over-year, reflecting continued deleveraging and a stable capital structure.
On the asset side, we saw improved working capital efficiency, with inventory reducing to ₹620 crores from ₹730 crores, and trade receivables declining to ₹631 crores from ₹696 crores.
Risks & challenges: Domestic revenue declined 4.5%, while exports were down 8% year - over-year.
The cost of raw material declined 9.5% year-over-year to ₹2,801 crores.
Other expenses declined 8.3% year -over-year to ₹441 crores, highlighting the continued focus on operational efficiency.
